children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my child Alex, who is 8 years old. I'm actually in the process of adopting him, but he hasn't come to live with me yet. I wanted to find out if I can claim Child Benefit now or if I need to wait until he moves in with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex.

This is an important question about the timing of Child Benefit claims during adoption. According to the rules, you can claim Child Benefit as soon as any child you're adopting comes to live with you - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, the child does need to have come to live with you first.

To clarify your situation:

**Has Alex already moved in to live with you, or is he still living elsewhere while the adoption process is ongoing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't moved in yet. He's still living elsewhere while we're going through the adoption process. Does that mean I can't claim Child Benefit at the moment?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex hasn't moved in with you yet.

Based on the Child Benefit rules, you would not be able to claim Child Benefit at this moment because Alex hasn't come to live with you yet. The rule states that you can claim Child Benefit as soon as the child you're adopting comes to live with you - but they do need to be living with you first.

However, once Alex does move in with you, you'll be able to claim Child Benefit right away without having to wait for the adoption process to be finalized.

Before I provide my final assessment, let me ask a few more questions to ensure I have a complete picture:

**When Alex does move in with you, will you be living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK now and will still be here when Alex moves in with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Do you expect to be responsible for Alex when he moves in - meaning you'll be living with him and providing for his needs (such as food, clothes, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Actually, even though he's not living with me yet, I'm already contributing towards his upkeep - I give £30 a week to help with his needs like clothes and things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information about your contributions towards Alex's upkeep.

That's a helpful detail. Let me ask one more clarifying question:

**Where is Alex currently living while the adoption process is ongoing? Is he living with foster carers, in residential care, with relatives, or in another arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living with foster carers at the moment while we go through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. 

Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's with the foster carers?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about the details of what the council is paying to the foster carers, to be honest. I just know that I contribute the £30 a week myself to help with his needs.

Thank you for all that information. I now have enough to provide you with an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation based on the rules:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16, so age-eligible)
- You're in the process of adopting him
- He hasn't moved in with you yet - he's still living with foster carers
- You live in the UK
- You're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep
- You're unsure if the local council is paying towards his accommodation or maintenance with the foster carers

The key rule here is that for adoption situations, you can claim Child Benefit as soon as the child you're adopting comes to live with you - but they do need to be living with you first. Since Alex hasn't moved in with you yet, you don't currently meet the basic residency requirement for claiming Child Benefit.

Additionally, there's uncertainty about whether the local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's with foster carers, which could also affect eligibility even if other conditions were met.
